safer-av · car maze Sim2Sim

Terminal-State-Aware Long-Horizon Sim-to-Real Evaluation: car maze

The toy study's maze, goals, costs and methods with a small car (1/10 scale) instead of a ball. A fixed controller drives through K goals. "Real" is the simulator with a weaker motor and brakes, less tyre grip and five wet patches; the downhill slopes are the same in both. Each method estimates the real cost of 936 evaluation goal sequences: 536 start at rest on a goal, 400 start while driving (where the real car is after 1–3 earlier goals). All numbers are averaged over 9 runs (3 data seeds × 3 model seeds).

Key results (K = 8, mean over 9 runs)
  • Direct's error is lower than every baseline's on Exposure, TTC at every n and for both start types: 5–36% below the best baseline.
  • Elsewhere a baseline is lower in some cells. Safety: Seg. outcome is lower at n = 200 (rest start) and n = 200, 400 (moving start). Path: Seg. outcome is lower at n = 200, 400, 600, 800, 1500 (rest start) and n = 200, 400, 600, 800, 1500 (moving start). Time: Seg. outcome is lower at n = 200, 400, 600 (rest start) and n = 200, 400 (moving start).
  • Against target-only (the same learning on real data only), Direct's error is: rest start Safety 23–48% lower; Exposure 26–48% lower; TTC 5–29% lower; Path 9% higher to 22% lower; Time 7–29% lower; moving start Safety 21–47% lower; Exposure 21–50% lower; TTC 11–30% lower; Path 8% higher to 24% lower; Time 14–26% lower.
  • Raw simulation has 2–31× Direct's error (it misses the sim–real gap). B1 and B2, which learn whole-sequence costs from the same real drives, have 1.3–9× Direct's error.
  • Ranking the scenes (Spearman correlation between estimated and true K=8 costs at n = 1000, range over costs and start types): Direct 0.92–0.99, target-only 0.91–0.99, raw sim 0.39–0.96.
  • Simulation-backed estimation (equal to Direct in expectation) is 43% higher to 22% lower than Direct across costs, start types and n.

Per-scene error

Mean absolute error between the estimated and the true real cost of each goal sequence. Raw sim: uncorrected simulation. Seg. outcome: segment-wise outcome correction (SCAPE-style). Target-only: backward Bellman learning on real data only. B1: direct regression of real returns. B2: route-level SCAPE. Direct: our main estimator. Sim-backed: our second evaluation mode (equal to Direct in expectation). Lowest error highlighted.

Limitations

  • Sim2Sim study (real = the simulator with changed physics) in one maze with 9 fixed goals and a hand-written controller.
  • Path and Time differ little between sim and real here (see "real vs sim" above), so raw simulation is already close on them.
  • The real physics and the controller were chosen with checks on separate queries (cost differences between scenes, sim–real gap and correlation, one-segment learnability) before any method was run; see README.md.

Per-run metrics (MAE, bias, RMSE, Spearman for every K and n): outputs/results/; means: outputs/report/summary.json.
